attempts.paper_title: Sizes and Shapes of Perivascular Spaces Surrounding Murine Pial Arteries
attempts.entry_title: Sizes and shapes of perivascular spaces around pial arteries (Raicevic et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: Several of the paper's central findings held in this data and several did not. The vessel radius peak near 28 um, the polynomial fit matching the segmented area ratio best, and the fit velocity ordering reproduced, mostly under only some analysis choices. The resistance power law held partially, while the area ratio and resistance distributions, ellipse parameters and PVS width asymmetry did not match. The likely reason is the paper's undescribed manual centerline cleaning and PVS selection, for which the agent used stand-ins. The validation against 2D images could not be tested because those images are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Raicevic, Forer, Ladron-de-Guevara, Du, Nedergaard, Kelley and Boster (2023) on dandiset 000491, which holds the 3D two-photon stacks and the final vessel and PVS segmentations of 14 pial artery segments in 9 mice. From the deposited segmentations it takes normal cross sections, measures PVS and vessel areas, fits the ellipse, spline and polynomial shapes and the vessel circle, and computes the hydraulic resistance per unit length, then compares the distributions with the paper's. The 2D time series used to validate the segmentation are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: After excluding cross sections near the edge of the imaging volume, each of the 14 PVS segments yields between 54 and 451 normal cross sections, about 0.8 um apart.
outcomes.source: Methods, Creating normal cross sections
outcomes.quote: This resulted in between 54 and 451 different cross sections for each of the 14 PVS segments that were included in the subsequent analysis. The average distance between normal planes was approximately 0.8 μ m.
outcomes.notes: No combination of P1, P2 and P4 holds. With the cleaned path (P2 a) and P4 b the segments give 202 to 604 cross sections at 0.648 um (mean spacing 0.876 um, within tolerance, but the most above 496.1) and 124 to 394 at 1 um (within the widened range, but spacing 1.345 um). With P4 a, 4 segments keep none. P2 b gives up to 78712 points per segment. The spacing is the mean step between neighbouring kept points (0.83 to 0.93 um per segment at 0.648 um). Before the revision after round 1, with the uncleaned path, the counts were 390 to 669 and 248 to 415. The cleaned path still meanders, 1.08 to 1.44 times the arc of the fitted centerline at 0.648 um at every location but E. Counted along the fitted centerline (a diagnostic in the notebook, with the share kept under P4 b), the segments would give 223 to 427 cross sections at each segment's own mean step (mean 0.876 um), 241 to 492 at the paper's 0.8 um, 219 to 447 at 0.88 um and 267 to 546 at 0.72 um; the first three are inside 48.6 to 496.1. The third verification did not accept these estimated counts as a test of the claim (no slices were taken along that path and its step was not measured), so the outcome stays not reproduced. Reference combination for measured values, P1 a (0.648 um), P2 a (cleaned longest path), P4 b (polynomial width), P5 a, P6 erosion 3, P7 b (outliers left out), unless stated.
deviations: Starts from the deposited final segmentations, as the claims file says; the vessel centerline is skimage's 3D thinning in place of MATLAB bwskel. Assumed, for the manual removal of erroneous points (Methods, Creating normal cross sections, "then manually removed erroneous points"), which the paper does not describe: the longest path through the skeleton (P2 a), less the points farther from the second-order polynomial fit of the centerline than the vessel radius (95th percentile of the vessel's inscribed radius along the path) and the points that revisit a stretch of the fitted centerline already passed (pvs.clean_path). Added after the first verification, which found the uncleaned path 1.28 to 2.24 times the distance between its ends; 7534 of 9564 path points are kept at 0.648 um and 4974 of 6010 at 1 um. Pixels in both the vessel and the PVS mask are counted as vessel. The Methods say overlaps were resolved by hand, case by case, but the deposited masks still overlap; the overlap exceeds 5% of the PVS in 381 of 6683 cross sections (P1 a, P4 b), 247 of them at J and 131 at E, so the choice is unlikely to change an outcome. The other assignment was not run.

Assumed, the PVS of a cross section is the two largest PVS regions (8-connected) that come within one vessel radius, sqrt(area / pi), of the vessel region, the vessel being the connected region at or nearest the slice center. The segmentation "removed ... all but the two largest regions in the PVS segmentation" (Methods, Segmentation) and the fits are of the lobes beside the vessel (Figure 4), while the deposited masks hold PVS around other vessels and far from the artery. Added after the first verification; before it all PVS pixels of the 332 um plane were used. By median area the lobes are 91 to 99% of a slice's PVS at every location but E (29 to 52%) and, at 1 um, H (70%). Cross sections with fewer than 20 vessel or PVS pixels have no fits (shown per location in the data check).

Assumed, planes where the deposited PVS mask covers more than 90% of the field are cleared before the cross sections are taken: at E and F the mask fills every plane below a depth (87 and 58 planes), and no plane of any other file is more than 50% PVS. Added after the first verification.

The edge distance of P4 is measured from the vessel center in the slice (circle fit, erosion 3), to which the Methods shift the slice ("The slices were then shifted so the center point of the vessel was located in the center of the image", Methods, Creating normal cross sections). Before the first verification it was measured from the skeleton point; the change is 0.75 to 3.85 um by median per location and keeps 6683 cross sections in place of 6665 (P1 a, P4 b).

proposed.reason: The criterion takes one slice per centerline point, so the count follows the length of the path. The cleaned path of this attempt, the stand-in for the paper's manual removal of erroneous points, is still 1.08 to 1.44 times the arc of the fitted centerline at 0.648 um (data check, as the verifier of round 2 found), and the voxel zigzag explains at most about 8% of that, so it holds more points than a centerline along the vessel. A centerline that follows the fitted curve is the better-supported reading of a hand-cleaned centerline. Counted along it with the share kept under P4 b (cell under cross-section-counts), P1 a gives 223 to 427 cross sections per segment at each segment's own mean step (mean spacing 0.876 um) and 241 to 492 at the paper's 0.8 um, both inside 48.6 to 496.1 with the spacing within tolerance, so the claim holds; P1 b still fails on its spacing (1.345 um). The margin is small: at a step of 0.72 um the most would be 546, and the counts are estimated from the kept share, not from slices taken along the fitted curve. The fewest, 223, is far above the paper's 54, which the criterion allows. The verifier of round 3 did not agree and would keep not reproduced: the counts come from scaling the kept share by the fitted arc over an assumed step, not from slices taken along a new path; a centerline that follows the fitted curve is a reading outside the claims file, which the Methods (points "manually removed" from the bwskel output) do not support; and the step of 0.876 um that passes is the mean step of the meandering path, not measured on a path along the vessel, while an average 26-connected step of about 0.73 um would give a most of about 539. The change could be considered if slices were taken along a path that follows the vessel, its own mean step met 0.72 to 0.88 um and the counts fell within 48.6 to 496.1; that analysis was not run and waits for a new attempt.

outcomes.quote: To consider the segmentation successful, at least 70% of the area had to overlap in both PVS and vessel ... The 3D segmentation and 2D segmentation match over 70% which gives confidence that 3D segmentation is accurate.

outcomes.source: Results, Area ratio, paragraph 2; Figure 5B and 5C

deviations: Starts from the deposited final segmentations, as the claims file says; the vessel centerline is skimage's 3D thinning in place of MATLAB bwskel. Added after the first verification, which found the uncleaned path 1.28 to 2.24 times the distance between its ends; 7534 of 9564 path points are kept at 0.648 um and 4974 of 6010 at 1 um. Cross sections are sampled by linear interpolation of the masks, thresholded at 0.5, on planes normal to the fitted centerline, one per path point, with pixels of the P1 voxel size, in place of MATLAB obliqueslice (a standard choice).

Pixels in both the vessel and the PVS mask are counted as vessel. The other assignment was not run.

Assumed, the PVS of a cross section is the two largest PVS regions (8-connected) that come within one vessel radius, sqrt(area / pi), of the vessel region, the vessel being the connected region at or nearest the slice center. The segmentation "removed ... all but the two largest regions in the PVS segmentation" (Methods, Segmentation) and the fits are of the lobes beside the vessel (Figure 4), while the deposited masks hold PVS around other vessels and far from the artery. Added after the first verification; before it all PVS pixels of the 332 um plane were used. By median area the lobes are 91 to 99% of a slice's PVS at every location but E (29 to 52%) and, at 1 um, H (70%). Cross sections with fewer than 20 vessel or PVS pixels have no fits (shown per location in the data check).

Assumed, planes where the deposited PVS mask covers more than 90% of the field are cleared before the cross sections are taken: at E and F the mask fills every plane below a depth (87 and 58 planes), and no plane of any other file is more than 50% PVS. Added after the first verification.

The edge distance of P4 is measured from the vessel center in the slice (circle fit, erosion 3), to which the Methods shift the slice ("The slices were then shifted so the center point of the vessel was located in the center of the image", Methods, Creating normal cross sections). Resistance is solved by finite differences on the pixel grid of the cross section, in place of finite elements (MATLAB solvepde). The domain is the region at least 1.5 pixels inside the mask's edge, which is the polygon through the boundary pixel centres after the Methods' one-pixel erosion. The Methods' check (a circle of the same area within 1% of the exact resistance) holds from 1000 um^2 at 0.648 um; at 300 um^2 and 1 um the error is 2.5%.

Assumed, within the vessel's horizontal extent, the polynomial fit's region runs from the line down to the vessel center height, minus the circle; the Methods and the claims file do not say how the region is closed across the vessel. The alternative was not run.

P4 reading (a), the horizontal extent of the PVS, keeps no cross section in 4 of the 14 segments (A, B, F, G), while the paper analysed all 14; its results are shown but it is the less supported reading.

The ellipse is fit to the region the PVS's outer boundary encloses, the PVS and vessel segmentations together with holes filled, as claims P9 has it since the answer of 2026-11-04. The crop window of each cross section now holds the whole ellipse; being larger, it also cuts less of the polynomial region at its edge, which moves the polynomial areas and resistances slightly; the values before the change are not in the notebook (with the reference combination and P9 a the polynomial area ratio now peaks at 1.684, median 1.710, table2).
Since the revision after round 1 the resistances and velocities of the fits are solved with the circle fit of every erosion of P6 (1, 3 and 5 pixels).

Location E is kept, as one of the paper's 14 segments, though its cleaned path follows a side branch of the vessel network in its mask, not the vessel with PVS beside it, and its lobes are 29 to 52% of the slice's PVS; it gives 202 of the 6683 cross sections (P1 a, P4 b). Neither keeping nor dropping it gives the paper's E. Added after the second verification, the notebook computes every claim's table again without E (the cell before the summary). Without E, no combination matches on linear bins and the polynomial is the closest for the largest share in all 96, as with E.

findings.statement: The single-plane time-averaged 2D images and their segmentations, which the Methods use to validate the 3D segmentation (at least 70% overlap for PVS and vessel), are not in the dandiset, so the validation cannot be checked.

The deposited vessel and PVS masks overlap in 11 of the 14 files (from 24 voxels at C to 344565 at E and 177417 at J), though the Methods say overlapping pixels were removed from one segmentation. The dandiset does not say which mask should take them.

At E and F the PVS mask fills every plane below a depth (87 and 58 planes, 98 to 99% of the field) and 50 to 60% of the whole volume, so it holds far more than the space beside the vessel. The dandiset does not describe this; this attempt clears those planes.

The vessel mask of E holds a network of branching vessels in one connected region, though the Methods say the vessels branching off the main vessel were removed by hand. The longest path through its skeleton runs through branches; after the cleaning of this attempt 361 of its 939 points (0.648 um) are kept, along a side branch, while the points removed run along the vessel with PVS beside it.

For L, M and N the reference_frame gives a depth step of 0.648 um, while the session descriptions say the planes are 1 micron apart. Vessel cross sections at the stated step are close to round (median height over width 0.91, 1.08 and 1.13), which is consistent with the reference_frame; the session descriptions appear to be wrong for these files.

The vessel channel (ChanA, described as FITC-dextran) has an emission wavelength of 698 nm and the PVS channel (ChanC) 525 nm, while the Methods say the green 525 nm channel holds the FITC-dextran. Every imaging plane names GFP as its indicator.
ChanB is described as injected fluorescent microspheres and its mask only as 'Segmentation masks for ChanB'; the paper mentions no microspheres, and L, M and N have no ChanB.
The subjects of locations A to D (BPN-OLD-M2 and BPN-OLD-M3) are 573 to 603 days old in the files, and most other subjects 76 to 113 days, while the Methods say all mice were 8 to 12 weeks old.
The first published version, 0.230427.1809, holds no PVS mask for L, M and N; version 0.230602.1307 adds them. The dandiset's description does not record the change.

disagreements.reason: The proposed counts (223 to 427, and 241 to 492) are not counts of slices; cell 12 computes each segment's count as (share kept under P4 b) times (arc of the fitted quadratic divided by an assumed step), and no centerline was built along the fitted curve. The claims file names two readings of P2, and under every combination of P1, P2 and P4 the claim fails. The proposal relies on a third reading, a centerline that follows the fitted curve, which the Methods do not support; they say only that erroneous points were "manually removed", and removing points does not move the rest onto a fitted curve. The quadratic is also smoother than the vessel, so the arc may understate the length of a correct centerline. The mean spacing of 0.876 um that passes is the mean step of the meandering path, which is circular; a 26-connected path at 0.648 um has an average in-plane step of about 0.73 um, which would give a most of about 539, above the limit. The change could be considered only if slices were taken along a path that follows the vessel, that path's own mean step met 0.72 to 0.88 um, and the counts then fell within 48.6 to 496.1.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors (left-right-no-difference), which test found no difference between the left and right PVS widths? Paired tests over all cross sections find one here (Wilcoxon p below 1e-29, KS below 1e-30), a test on the 14 per-segment medians does not (p 0.54 to 0.72 with all 14 segments).

Question for the authors (cross-section-counts and every pooled claim), how is the median PVS width of the edge exclusion measured? Taken as the horizontal extent of the PVS, it excludes every cross section in 4 of the 14 segments; taken as the polynomial-fit width, the segments keep 202 to 604 cross sections at 0.648 um, more than the paper's 54 to 451.

The paper's MATLAB code (segmentation, normal slices, fits, resistance) is not public, and the Methods leave open which centerline points were removed by hand, which PVS regions of a slice form its PVS, how the polynomial region is closed across the vessel and how each fit's edge points are chosen; the readings run here do not recover the paper's counts or most of its peaks.

Question for the authors (fig5bc-area-intersegment-variation), what shows that PVS area varies much more between segments than along each? The IQR of the 14 segment medians exceeds the median within-segment IQR (3260.3 against 1621.5 um^2), but the range of the medians (8461.9) is below the largest within-segment IQR (9476.5, H).

entries.title: Sizes and shapes of perivascular spaces around pial arteries (Raicevic et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Raicevic, Forer, Ladron-de-Guevara, Du, Nedergaard, Kelley and Boster (2023) on dandiset 000491, which holds the 3D two-photon stacks and the final vessel and PVS segmentations of 14 pial artery segments in 9 mice. From the deposited segmentations it takes normal cross sections, measures PVS and vessel areas, fits the ellipse, spline and polynomial shapes and the vessel circle, and computes the hydraulic resistance per unit length, then compares the distributions with the paper's. The 2D time series used to validate the segmentation are not in the dandiset.
